scope_note: DOCS-axis spine for ai-agent-cli, mined via the docs-surface lens (support/doc sections a mature ai-agent-cli ships (markdown headings)) from ['aider', 'gptme', 'openinterpreter']. Does NOT predict project-specific product direction — that is strategy, not completeness. An axis gates only after beating the generic-baseline control (check.py VALIDATED_GATING_AXES); the rest are advisory.

required.what: Prerequisites, installation paths, quickstart, and first successful run.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify there is a getting-started section that lists prerequisites, installation steps, a quickstart command, and an example showing a first successful run.

required.what: Supported install methods, optional extras, source installs, package managers, and platform notes.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find an installation matrix/table that compares supported install methods, package managers, optional extras, source installs, and platform-specific notes.

required.what: Config files, environment variables, model/provider defaults, and runtime options.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify a configuration reference exists listing config files, environment variables, provider/model defaults, and runtime options.

required.what: Core CLI workflows, example commands, interaction modes, and automation patterns.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find a usage guide with concrete CLI commands, interaction modes, workflow examples, and at least one automation/non-manual usage pattern.

required.what: Documented agent tools, computer-use features, MCP/ACP integrations, and supported actions.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify a tools/capabilities section documents agent tools, computer-use features, MCP/ACP integrations, and supported actions.

required.what: Non-interactive operation, agent creation, guardrails, monitoring loops, and stop conditions.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find an autonomous or non-interactive mode section covering agent creation, guardrails, monitoring loops, and stop conditions.

required.what: Local development environment, editable installs, dependency setup, and contributor bootstrap.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify a developer setup section explains local environment setup, editable installs, dependencies, and contributor bootstrap steps.

required.what: Contribution workflow, pull request expectations, issue reporting, and contributor rules.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find a contributing guide covering contribution workflow, PR expectations, issue reporting, and contributor rules.

required.what: Project style rules, language/version compatibility, organization conventions, and tactical implementation guidance.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify a coding standards section describes style rules, supported language/runtime versions, project organization conventions, and implementation guidance.

required.what: How to run tests, test expectations, assertions, flaky handling, and CI-oriented test workflows.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find a testing guide explaining how to run tests, expected assertions, flaky-test handling, and CI-oriented test workflows.

required.what: PR checks, CI failure classification, reruns, review handling, merge workflow, and release validation.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify a CI/PR operations section covers PR checks, CI failure types, reruns, review handling, merge workflow, and release validation.

required.what: Building docs, Docker images, binaries/packages, npm releases, and distributable artifacts.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find build/packaging instructions for docs, Docker images, binaries/packages, npm releases, or other distributable artifacts.

required.what: Docker-based development, isolated profiles, secure/customer environments, and container workflows.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify a containerized development section explains Docker-based development, isolated profiles, secure/customer environments, and container workflows.

required.what: Security policy, vulnerability reporting, safe operation, permissions, guardrails, and approval modes.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find a security/safety section covering vulnerability reporting, safe operation, permissions, guardrails, and approval modes.

required.what: Supported AI providers, model selection, local models, and model-specific configuration.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify a provider/model support section lists supported AI providers, model selection instructions, local model support, and model-specific configuration.

required.what: Plugins, skills, lessons, MCP support, web UI/server modes, and extension surfaces.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find an ecosystem/integrations section documenting plugins, skills, lessons, MCP support, web UI/server modes, or extension APIs.

required.what: Version history, news, changelog entries, and notable changes across releases.
required.day1_tell: Open the docs and find release notes or a changelog with version history, news, and notable changes across releases.
Open the docs and find a licensing section or LICENSE page that states the project license and legal-use terms.

optional.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify an FAQ exists with common questions about purpose, installation, providers, tools, comparisons, and usage.

optional.day1_tell: Open the docs and verify a community/links section lists community channels, demos, statistics, external links, or project discovery resources.
